title: Fingerprint and pin workflow for newly ingested models and automated performance-profile publishing
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Goal: Establish a deterministic fingerprinting + pin workflow for every model artifact we ingest (weights, tokenizer, config, quantization table), and wire an automated end-to-end publishing pipeline that produces certified performance profiles and docs pages for the model catalog. This ticket covers schema additions, CI/bench harness changes, publisher playbook, docs templates, and rollout gating checks.

Background: Recent onboarding runs showed inconsistency between model artifact hashes and the metadata stored in the catalog: some variants were missing provenance links, and performance profiles were published manually with varying benchmark parameters (sequence lengths, batching). That has led to ambiguous pins and unexpected regressions in customer workloads.

Scope (what we will deliver):
- New immutable fingerprint field (sha256) covering concatenated weight artifact checksum + tokenizer checksum + canonical config blob.
- Metadata additions: provenance_url, baseline_perf_id, supported_quant_bits, runtime_kernel_set, kv_cache_behavior, input_tokenization_checksum, default_sequence_profile, performance_publish_tag.
- A "pinflow": when a new model version is ingested the system will: compute fingerprint -> run gated benchmark suite (fast smoke then full suite) -> create performance profile document -> automatically publish profile to catalog draft -> add pin candidate. Manual approval required to finalize pin to "stable" and update routing rules.
- CI/bench harness updates: standardized load generator scenarios (latency-first, throughput-first), fixed seed prompts for deterministic P95/P99 measurement, and a canonical metric export format (CSV/JSONL).
- Docs: onboarding playbook page template, pinning FAQ, and a small migration guide for previously onboarded models lacking fingerprints.
- Rollout plan: start in staging for 2 weeks (canary ingestion path), then opt-in beta for dedicated customers, finally gated full rollout with automatic rollback on regression detection.

Non-goals: Not part of this ticket: UI/refactor of the Console's model page (separate DES ticket), long-term archival pipeline for raw artifacts.

Acceptance criteria:
- New fingerprint and provenance fields stored in catalog for all new ingests in staging.
- Bench harness returns structured profile with P50/P90/P95/P99 latency, tokens/sec, memory usage, and cost-estimate per-1M-tokens.
- Auto-generated docs page created alongside profile and linked from model catalog entry (draft state).
- Pin candidate is created and visible in pinning API; finalization requires a "pin-approve" action by a user with the model-owner role.
- Automated tests covering fingerprint calculation, profile schema compliance, and publishing flow included in CI.

Technical notes and decisions: 
- Fingerprint algorithm: SHA256 over a canonically serialized manifest: weights-s3-uri + size + weight-checksum, tokenizer-checksum, model-config-json (sorted keys), and quant-table-checksum (if present). This choice balances determinism and ease of recomputation during reingest.
- Store both fingerprint and component checksums (weights_checksum, tokenizer_checksum) to aid partial-validation and debugging.
- Performance harness: use an isolated per-ingest ephemeral cluster (small GPU pool) to run the fast smoke (30s) and full suite (3–6 min) depending on model size. Bench controller will tag results with sequence-profile labels (short/medium/long) and capture kernel selection info.
- Pin semantics: "candidate" pins are ephemeral and automatically expire after 30 days if not approved. Approved pins become immutable references used by routing and rollout APIs.
- Failure modes: bench failures mark the ingest as "needs-investigation" and attach logs & flamegraphs. A fallback path exists to publish metadata without a profile (explicit opt-out) but will mark customer_impact as "medium" and require a manual SLA acceptance.

Operational runbook (high level):
1) Ingest triggered -> fingerprint calculated -> artifacts stored in blobstore with fingerprint tag.
2) Bench pipeline executes smoke -> if pass, schedule full suite.
3) On success: publish profile, create draft catalog entry and pin candidate. Notify model-owner Slack channel.
4) Model owner reviews draft, approves pin via API or Console -> finalization updates routing.
5) On regression detected post-approval (automated quality monitors): trigger automatic fallback to prior pin and open ENG incident.

Migration guidance:
- Provide a backfill job to compute fingerprints for historical models. This job will be rate limited and annotated in the catalog as "backfill-2026-03". Backfilled models get a "needs-validation" flag and undergo a smoke bench run before being eligible for automatic pining.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How strict should fingerprint collision handling be? Current plan: treat collision as a hard error and require manual resolve; low probability but high impact.
- Cost of bench runs for very large models (>100B): propose a sampled-run policy (subset of scenarios) and a manual heavyweight-run opt-in.
